ev.q: The prevalence of current smoking increased from 27.5% in 1991 to 36.4% in 1997 and then declined significantly to 28.5% in 2001.
The prevalence of lifetime smoking, although stable through the 1990s, declined significantly from 70.4% in 1999 to 63.9% in 2001
28.5% of high school students are current smokers, and 13.8% are current frequent smokers.
During 2001, white and Hispanic students were significantly more likely than black students to report current smoking.
Among female students, a significant quadratic trend was detected, indicating that the prevalence of current smoking peaked during 1997--1999
Temporal changes were analyzed using logistic regression analyses that assessed linear and quadratic time effects simultaneously

Significant linear and quadratic trends were detected for lifetime, current, and current frequent smoking.

methods_quotes.q: Temporal changes were analyzed using logistic regression analyses that assessed linear and quadratic time effects simultaneously and that controlled for sex, race/ethnicity, and grade.
Data were weighted to provide national estimates, and SUDAAN was used for all data analysis.
